exercises.name: Isometric Neck Flexion
exercises.form_cue: Press forehead into palm. Resist — don't let head move. Hold 8-10 sec. Increase resistance gradually.
exercises.why: Progressive overload of deep cervical flexors. Higher hold duration builds endurance.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Extension
exercises.form_cue: Press back of head into palm. Resist evenly. Hold 8-10 sec. Increase push force vs Phase 1.
exercises.why: Progressive posterior cervical strength for the C5-6 segment.

exercises.name: Chin Tucks
exercises.form_cue: Sit tall. Draw chin straight back (double chin). Feel stretch at skull base. Do NOT tilt head down. Higher rep count builds endurance.
exercises.why: Higher volume chin tucks continue to decompress the C6 nerve root and build postural endurance.

exercises.name: Cervical Retraction with Overpressure
exercises.form_cue: Perform chin tuck, then use fingertips to gently push chin further back. Hold 5 sec.
exercises.why: Progressive decompression of the C5-6 foramen.

exercises.name: Scapular Squeezes
exercises.form_cue: Pinch shoulder blades together and DOWN. Hold 5 sec. Don't shrug. Higher volume for endurance.
exercises.why: Increased volume for upper back stabilizer endurance essential for running posture.

exercises.name: Prone Y-T-W Raises
exercises.form_cue: Face-down on bed, arms hanging off edge. Raise arms into Y, then T, then W. Thumbs up. Add light 0.5-1kg weights.
exercises.why: Progressive scapular stabilizer loading with added resistance.

exercises.name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Tilt head away from tight side. Gentle hand overpressure. STOP if radiating pain. Focus on LEFT side.
exercises.why: Maintenance of trapezius flexibility as strengthening increases.

exercises.name: Neck Lateral Flexion Strengthening
exercises.form_cue: Sit tall. Press side of head into palm (ear toward shoulder). Resist — don't let head move. Hold 5-7 sec each side.
exercises.why: Strengthens lateral cervical stabilizers (SCM, scalenes) to balance neck musculature and reduce side-bend compensation.

exercises.name: Thoracic Rotation
exercises.form_cue: Sit on chair, cross arms on chest. Rotate thoracic spine left and right. Keep hips facing forward. Hold end range 3 sec.
exercises.why: Improves thoracic mobility to reduce load transfer to cervical spine during running.

exercises.name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Straighten left arm, palm down. Use right hand to gently press hand down. Feel stretch on outer forearm.
exercises.why: Continued flexibility maintenance of the common extensor tendon.

exercises.name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Straighten left arm, palm up. Use right hand to press fingers back toward you.
exercises.why: Balances the forearm musculature and reduces tension through the elbow joint.

exercises.name: Eccentric Wrist Extensions (Light Dumbbell)
exercises.form_cue: Rest forearm on table, wrist over edge, palm down. Hold 1-2kg dumbbell. Use other hand to assist raising wrist up. Slowly lower under control (3-4 sec). The DOWN phase is the key.
exercises.why: Progressive eccentric loading with resistance stimulates stronger tendon collagen remodeling — key phase 2 progression.

exercises.name: Wrist Curls
exercises.form_cue: Rest forearm on table, wrist over edge, palm up. Hold 1-2kg dumbbell. Slowly curl wrist up (2 sec) and lower (3 sec).
exercises.why: Strengthens wrist flexors to balance the extensor loading and support elbow joint mechanics.

exercises.name: Band Wrist Extensions
exercises.form_cue: Anchor resistance band under foot. Hold band end in affected hand, palm down on thigh. Extend wrist up against band resistance. Slow return.
exercises.why: Band resistance provides progressive variable load through the wrist extension range — ideal for tendon loading.

exercises.name: Forearm Supination/Pronation
exercises.form_cue: Hold light dumbbell (1kg). Slowly rotate forearm palm-up then palm-down. Keep elbow at side.
exercises.why: Progressive rotator strengthening with resistance.

exercises.name: Grip Squeezes
exercises.form_cue: Squeeze a firm ball or grip trainer. Hold 3 sec. Release. Mild discomfort is OK, pain is not.
exercises.why: Progressive grip strengthening as tendon heals.

exercises.name: Dead Bugs (Alternating — Full Contralateral)
exercises.form_cue: Lie on back, arms up, knees at 90°. Extend opposite arm and leg fully — arm to ear, leg to floor (2cm above). Hold 1 sec. Return. Alternate. Keep lower back FLAT.
exercises.why: Progression from Phase 1: full contralateral extension challenges the deep stabilizers more, preparing for running gait.

exercises.name: Bird Dogs
exercises.form_cue: On all fours, extend opposite arm and leg. Hold 5 sec. Keep hips level — don't rotate. Add 1 sec pulse at end range.
exercises.why: Higher volume trains the posterior chain and anti-rotation stability.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridges
exercises.form_cue: Lie on back, feet flat. Extend one leg. Push hips up on single leg, squeezing glute. Hold 3 sec. Keep hips level.
exercises.why: Unilateral glute loading mimics single-leg stance in running and addresses left/right imbalances.

exercises.name: Side Planks
exercises.form_cue: Lie on side, elbow under shoulder, feet stacked. Lift hips off ground. Body forms a straight line. Hold 20 sec each side. Progress to 30 sec.
exercises.why: Lateral core stability is critical for running — prevents pelvic drop (Trendelenburg) that causes knee and IT band injury.

exercises.name: Pallof Press with Movement
exercises.form_cue: Stand sideways to anchor. Press band straight out from chest, then raise arms overhead, then return to chest. Resist rotation throughout. Both sides.
exercises.why: Dynamic anti-rotation training that progresses the Phase 1 Pallof Hold — builds rotational stability for running.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squats
exercises.form_cue: Feet shoulder-width. Sit back and down. Knees track over toes. Chest up. Full depth. Add tempo: 3 sec down, 1 sec up.
exercises.why: Higher volume and tempo squats build leg strength endurance for running.

exercises.name: Forward Lunges
exercises.form_cue: Step forward, lower back knee toward floor (2cm above). Push back to start through front heel. Alternate legs. Keep trunk upright.
exercises.why: Lunges replicate the single-leg loading of running — key progression for return to running preparation.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlifts
exercises.form_cue: Stand on one leg, soft knee. Hinge forward at hip, extending free leg behind. Keep back flat. Lower until you feel hamstring stretch. Return to upright.
exercises.why: Eccentric hamstring and glute loading in single-leg stance — directly trains the running posture and prevents hamstring injury.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raises
exercises.form_cue: Stand on one leg on edge of step. Rise up on toes, hold 2 sec, slowly lower below step level (3 sec down). Both feet for safety if needed.
exercises.why: Progression from bilateral calf raises. Single-leg replicates running load. The #1 progression for calf resilience.

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walks
exercises.form_cue: Place resistance band around ankles. Slight squat position. Step sideways — lead foot steps out, trail foot follows. Keep tension in band. 15 steps each direction.
exercises.why: Hip abductor (glute med) strengthening prevents lateral knee pain and IT band syndrome in runners.

exercises.name: Step-Ups (Higher Step)
exercises.form_cue: Use a sturdy step (20-25cm). Step up with one foot, drive through heel. Slow return. Alternate legs.
exercises.why: Progressed from Phase 1 with higher step height.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Half-kneeling position. Push hips forward. Squeeze glute of back leg. Feel stretch in front of hip. Add overhead reach for deeper stretch.
exercises.why: Continued hip flexor flexibility maintenance as lower body volume increases.

exercises.name: Single Leg Balance — Eyes Closed
exercises.form_cue: Stand on one leg, eyes closed. Hold 30 sec each side. Progress to unstable surface (folded towel).
exercises.why: Eyes-closed proprioception challenges the neuromuscular system more — critical for ankle stability on uneven terrain.

exercises.name: Towel Toe Curls
exercises.form_cue: Place towel on floor. Scrunch toes to pull towel toward you. Release and repeat. Higher rep volume.
exercises.why: Progressive intrinsic foot muscle strengthening for arch support.

exercises.name: Ankle Circles
exercises.form_cue: Seated. Lift foot off ground. Draw large circles with toes. 20 clockwise, 20 counter-clockwise each foot.
exercises.why: Increased ankle mobility range for running.

exercises.name: Short Foot Exercise — Standing
exercises.form_cue: Stand with foot flat. Try to shorten your foot by pulling ball of foot toward heel WITHOUT curling toes. Hold 5 sec. Progress to single-leg stance.
exercises.why: Progression to standing short foot — greater arch muscle load under bodyweight. Prepares for running arch demands.

exercises.name: Marble Pickups
exercises.form_cue: Sit with marbles (or small balls) on floor. Pick up each marble using only your toes. Place into a cup. Works all 5 toes.
exercises.why: Functional intrinsic foot strengthening — activates individual toe flexors and foot intrinsics for better toe-off power in running.
